the cross-sectional difference between historical volatility and implied volatility predicts the cross-sectional difference in option returns.

a zero-cost strategy that is long in the portfolio of delta-hedged options with a large positive difference between historical realized volatilities and at-the-money option implied volatilities, and is short in the portfolio with the opposite characteristic, produces an economically and significantly positive average monthly excess return.
